paragraphs.text: Attraction is an artifact type for nontraditional cards that begin the game in a dedicated side deck . Attractions are artifacts with no mana cost ; they aren't cast , and they never go to a player's hand .

The open an Attraction keyword action lets a player put the top card of their Attraction deck onto the battlefield face up under their control , and is the only way Attractions can enter play. A player who controls at least one Attraction rolls a six-sided die at the start of their precombat main phase , visiting ( triggering the "Visit" abilities of) any Attractions for which the number rolled is "lit up" (uniquely colored); this turn-based action is known as rolling to visit your Attractions. If an Attraction would leave the battlefield and go to any zone other than exile , it instead goes to the junkyard .

Attractions appear in Unfinity , where they represent top-down tropes from carnivals and amusement parks such as rides, games, and stands. Unfinity is the first Un-set to feature Eternal-legal cards ; while some Attractions feature an acorn stamp, the overall mechanic was intended to be tournament-legal, though oriented towards casual games. All Attraction-opening cards were ultimately banned from major formats in May 2024.

Attractions have a unique card frame with borderless art . The numbers 1 through 6 are listed from top to bottom on the right of the text box ; these are informally known as attraction lights. Attractions also have a unique card back , which welcome players to the Astrotorium and provide the rules for building an Attraction deck.

The Attraction deck is the collection of Attraction cards that a player plays with. In Limited formats ( Sealed Deck and Booster Draft ), an Attraction deck must contain at least three Attraction cards and may contain duplicates. In Booster Draft specifically, Attractions are drafted like other cards in the booster. A player who doesn't draft at least three Attraction cards cannot use an Attraction deck.

In Constructed formats, an Attraction deck must contain at least ten Attraction cards and must contain no more than one of each card with the same name, even if duplicates have different text or lights lit up. Due to this requirement, Attractions were not playable in Pauper even before their banning, as there are only eight common , Eternal-legal Attractions.

25 Attractions have the keyword ability prize, a reward for completing that Attraction's built-in minigame. When the prize is claimed, the Attraction is sacrificed , and its controller may open a new Attraction to replace it.
The following minigames provide prizes:

Cover the Spot — Drop three cards you own from outside the game one at a time onto the playing area from a height of at least one foot (about 0.3 meters). If those cards completely cover Cover the Spot, you win.
Dart Throw — Throw a card you own from outside the game onto the playing area from a distance of three feet (about one meter) . You win if that card touches Dart Throw.
Guess Your Fate — Look at the bottom of your library, then give a person outside the game a one-word clue, not on that card. They guess a word. If their guess appears in that card’s name, you win.
Memory Test — Name five exiled face-down cards, then look at them. If you named them correctly, turn them face up, and you win.

Pick-a-Beeble — Roll a six-sided die. Put a number of luck counters on Pick-a-Beeble equal to the result and create a Treasure token. Then if there are six or more luck counters on Pick-a-Beeble, you win.

Push Your Luck — Reveal cards from the top of your library until you decide to stop. If the total mana value of the cards revealed this way is 7 or less, create a 2/2 pink Teddy Bear creature token. If the total is exactly 7, you win.

Scavenger Hunt — Choose “<Quality A>,” “<Quality B>,” or “<Quality C>” at random. You have 10 seconds to search your library and reveal a card with the chosen item in its art. If you do, you win. Then shuffle.
Squirrel Stack — You have five seconds to stack dice on top of one another. If you stack at least five dice, you win.

The Superlatorium — An opponent chooses “<Quality A>,” “<Quality B>,” or “<Quality C>.” You choose a creature, then ask a person outside the game to choose the creature that best fits the chosen criteria. If they chose the same creature you chose, you win.

Trivia Contest — An opponent chooses “<Quality A>,” “<Quality B>,” or “<Quality C>”, then mills a card. You have ten seconds to name something from the chosen category that starts with the same letter as the milled card. If you do, you win.
Early in design, when an Attraction was open, all players could visit it, not just the Attraction's controller.

Different variants of the same Attraction may have different lights lit up. The number 1 will never be lit up, and the number 6 will always be lit up. There are sufficient common and uncommon variants to have all combinations of the four intermediate numbers printed, each with unique flavor text if applicable. For example, if an attraction only has two lights active, there are four variants. This is also true for those with four lights, and those with three lights have six variants. Rare attractions have only two variants each, aside from the unique Ferris Wheel , but they "pair up" to represent all numbers equally across all rares.

Approximately half of the Attractions printed in Unfinity are acorn cards , making them unusable for official tournament play. However, the other half are non-acorn, as are most non-Attractions that open Attractions. It was thought that the lower power level of the Attraction mechanic as well as stickers from the same set would prevent their side deck requirements from being a burden in competitive play, while still being an occasional surprise at that level and encouraging players to use them in more casual play.

Despite the design intentions, even the relatively low tournament usage of certain cards, particularly the sticker card _____ Goblin , required those players to maintain appropriate side decks. Furthermore, players using decks without sticker cards but with control-stealing effects felt pressured to maintain the same side decks to avoid any chance of missed advantage. In May of 2024, it was decided that the burdens of these side decks were too great, so all cards that bring stickers or Attractions into the game were banned in Legacy , Vintage , and Pauper.
